title: Zelensky and European leaders meet Trump at the White House on security guarantees
body:
On 18 August 2025, US President Donald Trump hosted Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House, three days after Trump's summit with Vladimir Putin in Alaska. A group of European leaders joined the meeting: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.

The main topics were security guarantees, territory and a ceasefire. Europe would serve as the first line of defence for Ukraine, with the United States helping mainly by selling weapons, and Trump would not say whether US troops would be involved. Trump raised possible land exchanges based on the current front line, which Zelensky opposes. Trump had shifted toward seeking a full peace agreement rather than a ceasefire, while Merz and Macron urged a ceasefire.

Trump said he had spoken with Putin and "began the arrangements for a meeting" between Zelensky and Putin at a location to be determined. He said he would then meet both leaders, with no date given, and that a trilateral meeting gave a "reasonable chance" of ending the war. Zelensky thanked Trump for his personal efforts and agreed to a possible trilateral meeting. He described his one-on-one meeting with Trump as constructive.

No ceasefire and no territorial agreement were reached. The meeting was widely contrasted with the confrontation in the Oval Office on 28 February.
